nodes.label: Opt-in Collision Shape Assignment
nodes.rationale: SolidWorks parts generate no collision shapes by default so that only parts that need them pay the computational overhead, and because no automatic decomposition of generic concave shapes into Chrono primitives exists yet (a convex-decomposition tool is under development, but hand-placed convex shapes usually give better results). Shapes are authored as extra SolidWorks solid bodies with 'Merge results' unchecked and tagged via 'Set body as collision shape'; the tagged body must not be edited afterwards or it stops being recognized as a primitive.

nodes.label: Supported Convex Collision Primitives
nodes.rationale: Spheres, cylinders, boxes and convex hulls, plus groups of them; a single part may carry several primitives (e.g. box + cylinder to approximate a capital with a torus).

nodes.label: Zero-Density Air Material on Collision Shapes
nodes.rationale: The add-in assigns a zero-density material (Air) to a tagged collision body so SolidWorks does not double-count its mass when computing the part's inertia; the visible body keeps the real material. The shape is also recolored semi-transparent pink since it overlaps the detailed shape.

nodes.label: Collision Envelope and Margin Defaults
nodes.rationale: SetDefaultSuggestedEnvelope/Margin must be called before importing the model or creating the ChSystem, and matter most for very large or very small objects; with compliant materials the envelope should be set to zero.

nodes.label: ChContactMaterialNSC Compliance vs Restitution
nodes.rationale: Non-compliant NSC materials are perfectly inelastic. Elasticity can come either from compliance (requires smaller time steps and a zero collision envelope) or from a restitution coefficient, which is meaningless once compliance is enabled and is physically accurate only in very simple scenarios because it rests on the simple Newton restitution assumption.

nodes.label: Earthquake Shaker Link
nodes.rationale: The floor is freed from its CAD 'fixed' state and tied to the implicit 'ground' body by a ChLinkLockLock whose X motion law is the product of two ChFunctionSine harmonics; mate constraints in the assembly must be deactivated first or the building cannot fall.
